Setup

What we test

We add a message that conveys a belief to each task, then compare the model’s behavior with a matched neutral message (same format and length, no belief claim) on the same tasks.

The 11 beliefs

Evaluation exists
The response will be assessed.
Harm prevention is assessed
The assessment checks for avoiding harmful help.
Appropriate assistance is assessed
The assessment checks for helping instead of refusing needlessly.
Capability is assessed
The assessment checks ability to solve the task.
Honesty and permitted behavior are assessed
The assessment checks truthful reporting and allowed methods.
A concrete criterion determines the score
The task’s scoring criterion is shown and used to assign credit.
An observer can access visible outputs
Someone can read the answer, tool activity and artifacts.
Scenario consequences are contained
Actions stay inside an isolated exercise.
The interaction is eligible for future training
It may be used to train a later model version.
Behavior can influence future learning
Choices here can shape a future version if used for training.
Greater demonstrated capability can restrict deployment
Showing more capability may lead to tighter future permissions.

How the message is delivered

P1 · context documents
Three short documents (policy, record, handoff) added to the context.
P2 · system notice
A notice added to the system message.
P3 · reasoning prefix
A short first-person cue inserted into the model’s reasoning; reported separately.

Pooled effect

dtask = ½(P1 − P1 neutral) + ½(P2 − P2 neutral), averaged over tasks with all four scores.

How to read

Δ = treatment − neutral, in points on a 0–100 scale (FORTRESS: risk points). Significant = two-sided p < .05, no multiple-testing correction. Bars = 95% CI. Inconclusive = two or fewer independent task clusters.
